newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Drugs found beneath Venezuela earthquake ruins.
newsitem.headline: Drugs found beneath Venezuela earthquake ruins.

text.p: Venezuelan rescue workers looking for dead bodies among the ruins of a building flattened by a powerful earthquake last week made an unexpected discovery on Monday -- 22 packets of drugs presumed to be cocaine, authorities said.

District attorney Jose Francisco Molina said the drugs were discovered beneath the mound of concrete and steel that was once an eight-story building in Cumana 155 miles (410 km) east of Caracas. Officials did not disclose the quantity or value of the drugs haul.
A wallet containing papers belonging to a Colombian and a Peruvian was found nearby, he told Radio Caracas Radio.
The building, from which the bodies of a 27-year-old woman and her one-year-old baby girl were also pulled on Monday, had housed several offices and a few private apartments.

The quake last Wednesday -- Venezuela's deadliest for three decades -- flattened schools and homes, killing at least 76 people and injuring more than 500. Many of the dead were children, crushed in their classrooms as they took end-of-term exams.
Although not a major drugs producer Venezuela has become an important transit route for drugs from neighbouring countries to the United States and Europe.
